newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: TEN STATE HEADS EXPECTED AT VILNIUS CONFERENCE.
newsitem.headline: TEN STATE HEADS EXPECTED AT VILNIUS CONFERENCE.

text.p: Lithuanian President Algirdas Brazauskas said on Thursday that as many as ten Eastern European presidents will attend a conference in Vilnius in September aimed at fostering good neighbourly relations.
Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin is also due to go to the meeting, which will take place on September 5 and 6.

"It is almost certain that the conference will be attended by the presidents of Romania and Bulgaria and it is highly probable that the presidents of Slovakia and Hungary will arrive too," Brazauskas told the news conference.
The presidents of Finland, Ukraine, Poland, Belarus, Latvia, Estonia and Chernomyrdin have already said they will attend.
"It ( the conference) is not aimed at the creation of a new political structure," Brazauskas said.
Brazauskas said the main goal of the event was to develop regional cooperation but there were no initial plans to sign a joint document or to make a joint declaration.
"We came to the conclusion that it is hardly possible, though attempts have been made," Brazauskas said.
The conference follows NATO's invitation to Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary to begin accession talks.
Russia which has grudgingly accepted the expansion of the alliance into Central Europe but has strong objections to the entry of former Soviet republics.
